Genuinely GREATLY Let down by this game. 

I wanted to love Squad. On paper, it sounds like everything I’ve wanted out of a tactical shooter — teamwork, communication, realism, coordination, and intense firefights where strategy actually matters. Instead, what I got was one of the most frustrating multiplayer experiences I’ve had in years.

The biggest issue? Communication is practically dead unless you’re lucky enough to land in the perfect server at the perfect time. This is a game BUILT around teamwork and voice communication, yet half the matches feel like you’re dropped into total silence. Nobody talks, nobody coordinates, nobody listens. And when people DO finally start talking, half the time I can’t even understand them because nobody is speaking English on the servers I keep getting thrown into.

I don’t care where people are from — genuinely. But if the entire game depends on communication and coordination, there has to be better server organization or filtering. It becomes impossible to enjoy a tactical game when every squad sounds like six different conversations happening in languages you don’t understand while the squad leader blasts music into the mic and drives a transport truck straight into an ambush.

Then there’s the community side of things, which somehow manages to be even worse. I’ve heard people openly praising or joking about genuinely heinous extremist groups and violent ideologies during gameplay, and way too often nobody even bats an eye. Instead of getting shut down, it gets laughed off like “edgy humor.” It completely kills the atmosphere and makes the community feel toxic in a way that goes beyond normal online trash talk.

And that’s what irritates me most: Squad SHOULD be incredible. The gunplay can feel immersive. The sound design is fantastic. Some moments genuinely feel like you’re inside a war movie. But those moments are buried under poor communication, disconnected teammates, dead squads, language barriers with no good matchmaki…

claims.claim: Performance and optimization are poor following the engine upgrade to UE5.

citations.review_text: The optimization has gone way down. I played the game some years ago before it got the big engine overhaul to UE5 and it was fantastic and smooth. Now with the new engine it's not any prettier and it's a whole lot laggier. I specifically wanted to play this game again cause I figured it could run on my older PC as I, like a lot of people, wait for parts to go down in pricing. I was disappointed to see they decided to in the midst of poorly optimized games to join the bandwagon of producing even more poorly optimized games. If they ever elect to really dig down to make their game less of a resource hog I would gladly change my review because the ACTUAL game once able to be accessed is fantastic.

Amazing realism. Terrible optimization. 😅 My biggest issue isn't even the performance—it's the lack of meaningful official content. The default game modes and missions feel neglected, almost like they were left unfinished. Squad is an incredible foundation, but it deserved much better post-launch support. 🎮
I feel this game is extremely boring and unoptimized. From my perspective not worth the asked price.

Bought this game years ago, and I wish I didn't. Picked it up again recently, and I'm blown away at how it still feels like an early access game. Nothing feels polished at all. Not to mention this game runs on UE5 now, and to the surprise of no one, runs horribly.

I came into Squad expecting something close to ARMA, where I’ve logged thousands of hours. That expectation was a mistake — these games aim for different experiences, and Squad doesn’t deliver what ARMA players might expect.

The pacing is one of the biggest issues. You can spend 10–15 minutes just getting to the frontline, only to die quickly and repeat the process. That might be acceptable if the combat felt rewarding — but it doesn’t.

Weapon handling feels off. Scopes, especially for marksman/sniper roles, are underwhelming — limited zoom and awkward visual scaling make long-range engagement frustrating rather than satisfying. Gunplay overall lacks precision, which is a serious problem in a game that leans heavily on realism.

The UI and controls don’t help either. Basic actions like switching weapons or managing loadout feel unnecessarily clunky. The lack of intuitive key bindings and smooth inventory interaction adds friction where there shouldn’t be any.

To be fair, the game does have strengths — sound design, teamwork emphasis, and some aspects of realism are solid. But they don’t compensate for the core gameplay issues.

Bottom line: if you’re expecting an ARMA-like sandbox, this isn’t it. For me, it ended up feeling like a poor trade-off between realism and playability. I would have been better off going with Arma Reforger.

After 4 hours in Squad, I’m uninstalling.

The result is a game where the time investment is high, but the payoff isn’t. I can see the intention — teamwork, realism, slower pacing — but the execution makes it feel more frustrating than rewarding.

I’d rather spend my time in Arma, where the balance between realism and playability works better for me.

The game takes some learning, and nothing's wrong with that. The learning curve isn't too steep outside of certain vehicles and mechanics - Which many lobbies will require you to have X amount of hours training on that particular vehicle before you can even think about touching it. The community? Well, very hit and miss. These days it seems more miss than anything. For a game that likes to talk about communication being key, there certainly isn't a whole lot of it. Even on the " Beginner Friendly " servers there's not much of it going on, which doesn't help the new folks who are trying to get into the game. There's also quite a number of hackers in the game also, so that's a thing, unfortunately.

The gameplay is okay and decently responsive, feeling weighty but not clunky outside of stance change, vaulting, and vehicle and loadout manipulation. Okay, that means half the total movement and interactions are clunky. Whoops, but true. The vehicle damage system is absolutely horrendous and it's frankly insulting that it's so bad. As much as I hate to mention War Thunder - Squad could learn at least 2 things from the damage model system. Especially since the combat in this game is supposed to feel respectably authentic and realistic. Then there's the game's lack of optimization and performance issues even on medium and low settings. 

It's one of those games that is best played with some friends rather than solo. Solo playing simple isn't ideal because you just can't count on your random teammates to help you when you need it. Playing with friends, I wasn't let down. Randoms, I was. There isn't much cohesion at all in Squad these days.

claims.claim: Players report microphone and voice chat issues that prevent communication, which is considered essential for the game.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to enjoy Squad, but after hours of troubleshooting I still can’t get my microphone to work. I use a SteelSeries Arctis 7+, and the mic works perfectly everywhere else, including Windows and every other game I own. I’ve tried changing input devices, setting it as the default communication device, checking Windows permissions, verifying game files, reinstalling, and following every fix I could find. Nothing works.

After digging around, it’s clear I’m not the only one. There are countless comments on YouTube and forum posts from people dealing with the exact same issue, especially with headsets that work flawlessly outside of Squad. Communication is the core of this game, so when voice chat doesn’t work, it ruins the experience.

Until this issue is properly addressed, I can’t recommend Squad to anyone.

Even on the " Beginner Friendly " servers there's not much of it going on, which doesn't help the new folks who are trying to get into the game. There's also quite a number of hackers in the game also, so that's a thing, unfortunately.

The gameplay is okay and decently responsive, feeling weighty but not clunky outside of stance change, vaulting, and vehicle and loadout manipulation. Okay, that means half the total movement and interactions are clunky. Whoops, but true. The vehicle damage system is absolutely horrendous and it's frankly insulting that it's so bad. As much as I hate to mention War Thunder - Squad could learn at least 2 things from the damage model system. Especially since the combat in this game is supposed to feel respectably authentic and realistic. Then there's the game's lack of optimization and performance issues even on medium and low settings. 

It's one of those games that is best played with some friends rather than solo. Solo playing simple isn't ideal because you just can't count on your random teammates to help you when you need it. Playing with friends, I wasn't let down. Randoms, I was. There isn't much cohesion at all in Squad these days.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance drops, frame rate issues, and constant stuttering following the Unreal Engine 5 update.

citations.review_text:
Loved this game. Supported it since it was in closed alpha because I was close to the original devs (modders  that created Project Reality). Those guys are long gone, and the company changed a lot. So, it breaks my heart to say that you should no longer buy this game. Some bugs from the early days are still there - even though they switched to UE5... And dont get me started on UE5.. the game still looks like it's been made 20 years ago, but now it has the performance of UE5 with it's constant frame drops etc.. On the other hand, OWI (devs) STILL haven't delievered on all the promises from the original kickstarter campaign... but they did have enough time to pick up a couple of military contracts in the meantime.

The game is jank, it's clunky, it has no idea what it wants to be after all these years, and the devs made a ingenious decision to rework the scopes.. so now, unlike any other game, when you ADS with a scope, all that happens is that your whole screen blurs out, and then only the middle of it is visible and the scope itself shows the zoomed in picture.. So basically 95% of your screen blurs out, and doesn't zoom (like getting your eye closer to the scope) but instead only the middle of the screen is occupied with the scope that zooms in like.. idk 2x or whatever.
Don't get me started on the intro video that YOU CANNOT SKIP. The only way to skip it is to delete it from the game files, but when you verify the files (and you'll do that almost every other time a server crashes) you need to delete it again.. Not only that the intro video is LOUD af, but it's like 4 minutes long. So every time you boot up the game you have to sit there and do nothing.


With all the things like that, it has become literally unplayable. And trust me, those things will NEVER get fixed, because 7 year old bugs/issues never got fixed/resolved.

So yeah, don't buy ANY of their products.

also slideshow on sanxian pls fix

I cannot stress enough how bad the state of the game is with bugs and broken gameplay, tanks stuck in the ground, vehicles handle horribly somehow there is both massive understeer and massive oversteer. Gunplay is atrocious it feels like I'm playing as a child soldier instead of a, supposedly, professional infantryman. The devs claim they sped up the ADS animation but they added a little wobble at the end that completely cancels out the change and makes it even worse than before. This problem is exaggerated when using binoculars or AT weapons. 

Non-existent optimisation on UE5 and constant graphical glitches and rgb strobelights dancing on screen in low light areas and black boxes on AMD GPU's...how is this the only UE5 game that I own that performs horribly??? Devs live in their own bubble it seems like and just ignore player feedback because it feels like nothing from the surveys they had was implemented the way it was supposed to be but instead they passed it around to their "F*ck it up" department before it reached actual programmers. 

1.2k hours but holy hell has my patience run out

Just buy Arma instead

5k hours so think Im in an informed position to comment - 3.5k gaming around 1.5 admin and seeding
Pre-ICO gameplay was more realistic than the post ICO nonsense the short sighted developers forced on the community. 2-3 years of "we wont change it" from the developers and consequential fallout from the community, the developers have finally got with the program and reworked the game again in the latest update. At the same time they introduced controller support which Im not sure anyone asked for, and in doing so removed half of the customisation for key binds and input sensitivity.

Performance is terrible, on med-high settings im lucky to see 50 frames with a 4080. There has been no tangible improvement to performance in the last 3 years, if anything with the move to UE5 performance dropped.

The devs themselves seem to be lacking basic project management ability, patches rollout which break the game and need to be rolled back. As an example rolling out a patch which turned materials and shades inside out

Things the community has been asking for for years:
Fastropes
improved heli flight model
OPTIMISATION

What we got:
DLC (paid for) weapon skins

i enjoy this game greatly. its very fun. if you like hell let lose or arma this is a great game. its not as micro as arma. but still needs more thought than a normal FPS. but negative because after this update my performance has been destroyed. i used to get 50-90 fps on high settings. after update it went down to 10-30. i had to set my settings to low to keep it over 30. and if there are too many trees and explosions ill go down to 20. my specs arent the best. but this is unacceptable.
(after checking the specs i see i just barely exceed the recommended specs. frankly these specs are the minimum to actually play the game. anything lower and you can only load the game.)

Good game, bad review because of it's performance. Bought the game prior to UE5, now I have to resort to spells, witchcraft and dark rituals to (maybe) get 30FPS. Game needs far more optimization rather than upgraded graphics, this is an old game afterall.
